chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baghdadi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Zayd, who raised the hadith (to the Prophet) saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'A dirham spent on dyeing (hair) is superior to spending a thousand dirhams in the way of Allah. And in it are fourteen benefits: it drives away wind from the two ears, removes the film from the sight, softens the nostrils, improves the scent, strengthens the gums, removes the odor of the armpits, reduces the whispering of Satan, the angels rejoice in it, the believer rejoices in it, and it irritates the disbeliever. And it is a adornment, a fragrance, and a deliverance for him in his grave, and Munkar and Nakir (the interrogators in the grave) will be shy of it.'

key_terms.الرِّيحَ: Wind (often referring to ear issues or internal wind)
key_terms.مُنْكَرٌ وَنَكِيرٌ: Munkar and Nakir (the two angels who question the dead in the grave)

ai.seo_question: What are the fourteen benefits of dyeing hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith elevates the Sunnah of hair dyeing from mere grooming to a spiritually potent act, asserting its merit exceeds that of substantial charitable spending. The text details fourteen benefits, blending physical hygiene with metaphysical effects, such as pleasing angels and causing the grave interrogators Munkar and Nakir to feel shy, thereby linking personal adornment to eschatological comfort.
